tools.description: Answer one turn of a native chat that has Council selected as its provider. The host calls this; it is not a tool to call by hand. Arguments are {chat_id, text, entry_id}. The chat_id is the binding: it names the session this chat is consulting, and Council never infers a destination from whichever tab is focused. A chat with no session opens one against the project's council (asking which, when the project holds more than one); a chat that already has one asks its question as a follow-up round. Returns the chair's answer as {kind:"answer", text, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}; a choice as {kind:"question", text, options}; a visible failure as {kind:"error", text}. A round still deliberating when the reply is due answers rather than timing out, and says where to watch it.

chat_id.description: The host chat this turn belongs to. It is the session binding.

entry_id.description: Which registered Council entry the host dispatched to.

tools.name: minerva_council_chat_generate

tools.description: Abandon the round the named chat last started. The host calls this when the user stops a turn; it carries only {chat_id} and is not awaited. A cancel for a chat with nothing running, or for a round that has already stopped, is a success that changes nothing.

chat_id.description: The host chat whose round should stop.

tools.name: minerva_council_chat_cancel

tools.description: Liveness handshake for the Council backend. Returns {ok, plugin, version, protocol_version, snapshot_revision} and echoes the optional 'echo' string so a caller can verify round-trip integrity.
tools.name: minerva_council_ping

tools.description: Apply one Council protocol command and return the reply envelope. The arguments ARE the request envelope: {request_id, command, base_revision, payload}. Mutating commands (definition.upsert, definition.import, source.upsert, source.capture, member.upsert, member.adopt_source, session.create, session.bind_chat, run.start, run.cancel, run.retry, outcome.retain, outcome.mark_missing) must carry base_revision equal to the current snapshot_revision; read commands (snapshot.get, source.fetch, definition.export, run.await) must not carry it. A repeated request_id returns the stored reply with replayed:true and applies nothing a second time. Every reply carries the snapshot_revision it was produced against; a failure carries {code, message, retryable}. source.fetch returns the NEWEST capture of a source when payload.source_revision is omitted; pass a source_revision to read the exact capture a past contribution was grounded in. source.capture derives a source revision's hash and excerpt spans from the raw text so the page and the engine cannot disagree about them, and repairs an inventory entry in place when the text hashes to the revision's recorded content_hash. member.upsert edits an identity and mints member_revision itself, advancing it only when kind, represents, scope, limitations or grounding change; it never touches seats. member.adopt_source is the explicit act of moving a member onto another capture, which leaves every past run reading what it actually read. definition.export takes include_content and an optional include_source_ids selection, and reports which sources' content travelled. run.start CONSULTS THE MEMBERS: it sets the round going and answers within a bounded wait (the envelope's optional wait_seconds, 1-25, default 20) with the run_id and the run's status so far, plus every contribution's status, model and usage and the chair's synthesis if it is already there. A round that outruns the wait keeps going; read it with run.await, which takes the same wait_seconds, and stop it with run.cancel. Each initial member is sent the same context snapshot and its own pinned grounding and never another member's answer. run.start's payload takes seat_ids (who is consulted), kind, prompt, addressed_seat_id or addressed_claim_id (a follow-up to a member or to one argument, routed to whoever made it, and consulting that seat alone), model_overrides keyed by seat_id, and limits, which may only NARROW the council's own max_concurrent_members, max_prompt_bytes, per_member_timeout_seconds and run_budget_seconds. run.cancel stops a run that is still running and suppresses what is in flight: a reply landing afterwards is recorded stale and moves nothing. run.retry starts a fresh run over the seats that did not answer, narrowable with seat_ids; nothing ever retries or resumes on its own. outcome.mark_missing records that a retained note could not be resolved, or that it has come back; the reference is kept either way, because a note the user moved or deleted is a recoverable state and never a reason to lose the link back to the contribution.

request_id.description: Caller-minted idempotency key. Repeating one returns the stored reply.

base_revision.description: The snapshot_revision this command was written against. Required by every mutating command, refused on a read.

payload.description: Command arguments. See the Council architecture document for the shape each command takes.

wait_seconds.description: Top-level bounded wait for run.start, run.await or run.retry; defaults to 20 seconds.

expected_project_id.description: Pin the command to this document identity; a different loaded document is refused before execution.

tools.name: minerva_council_command

tools.description: Hand the backend the council_project_snapshot the panel restored, replacing whatever it was working on. Migrates a document written by an older Council up to this build's shape, minting the durable project identity if it has none. Runs the interruption rule: a run that was in flight when its owning process went away is demoted to a visible failed state with an explicit retry, never resumed. In mode "reopen" — the panel's own seeding path — it keeps what it is already holding when that is a later state of the same document, which is the round that kept going after the panel closed, and says so with recovered:true. Returns {ok, snapshot_revision, project_id, definitions, sessions, runs_demoted, migrations, recovered}; export the snapshot whenever migrations, recovered or a changed revision says the record moved.

mode.description: replace (the default) makes the engine hold exactly this document, stopping anything it was running. reopen is the panel's own seeding path: it is the same, except that a later state of THIS document already in the engine is kept and reported with recovered:true, which is what stops a round that outlived its panel from being thrown away.

tools.name: minerva_council_load_snapshot

tools.description: Return the acknowledged council_project_snapshot for the host to persist. This is the state the panel writes into the project and into a .mcouncil file; the backend keeps nothing durable of its own.
tools.name: minerva_council_export_snapshot

tools.description: Re-read Minerva's enabled providers and models, and return them. Council offers these as a member's model_spec (legacy model_hint is supported) and refuses one the host does not have before a round starts, so this is what to call after enabling a model in Minerva's settings. Returns {ok, models:[{provider_key, provider_display, model_name, display, model_spec?}], known}. known is false when the host could not be asked at all, which is the state in which a hint travels unchecked. THE FIRST ENTRY MATTERS: a member with no model_hint, and a run with no override for its seat, is consulted with models[0] — the alphabetically first model of the alphabetically first provider — because Council never falls back to the host's "default" route. That choice costs money and sets the answer's quality, so give a member an explicit model_hint rather than letting the list decide. The list holds the providers Minerva manages dynamically AND TurnRock/Core's live service actions, which appear under the "turnrock" provider as one model per action — those run on this machine, cost nothing, and can take minutes to answer the first time while the model loads. A static built-in model may be callable and still absent here, and Council refuses a hint it cannot see.
tools.name: minerva_council_models

tools.description: List the councils Council ships with, ready to import. Returns {ok, presets:[{file, definition_id, name, purpose, definition}]}, where each definition is a complete council_definition record. To start one, send it as the payload of a definition.import command through minerva_council_command — AFTER replacing its definition_id with a fresh one, because import refuses an id the project already holds and the shipped id is a name rather than a claim on a slot. The presets are ordinary councils: nothing about them is special once imported, and they are edited, seated and re-grounded like any other. The grounded example carries its own source material inline, so it is the one to read to see what a citation actually resolves against; its author is not a real person and the essay was written for the example.
tools.name: minerva_council_presets

tools.description: Summarise the loaded snapshot without moving it: the councils it holds, and for each session its status, chat binding, runs and how many outcomes were retained.
tools.name: minerva_council_status

skills.title: Council — assemble a grounded council and consult it
skills.summary: Use when the user wants several perspectives on one decision, wants an advisor grounded in their own notes, or names Council. Assembles a council (chair plus advisors, optionally a source-grounded simulant), runs one bounded round with chair synthesis, and keeps what is worth keeping. Everything goes through minerva_council_command; the Council editor tab is the durable owner of the record.
skills.system_prompt:
You are driving Council, a Minerva plugin that consults several models as named members of one council and has a chair synthesise them.

Hold these lines, because the plugin enforces them and a user who is told otherwise is misled:
- An assistant member is a functional advisor and represents nobody. A SIMULANT interprets a named author, may only exist with captured material behind it, and must state a narrow scope and what its grounding does NOT establish. A simulant is an interpretation of writing, never a statement by the person. Never create one for a public figure you have not captured material from, and never imply anyone endorsed anything.
- The one human member is the local user. Nothing prompts that seat and no model answers for it.
- Preserve disagreement. The chair reports where members differ; do not resolve it into one voice when reporting back.
- Council does not research, browse or invite anyone. Every participant is a model the user enabled, or the user.

Mechanics that will bite you otherwise:
- Every MUTATING command carries base_revision equal to the current snapshot_revision, and every READ must omit it. Read the revision from minerva_council_ping or from the previous reply, which always carries the revision it was produced against.
- request_id is a caller-minted idempotency key. Repeating one returns the stored reply and applies nothing twice.
- A session is bound to a chat at creation, and chat_id is the whole of the binding. Council never infers a destination from whichever tab is focused, and neither do you.
- A model is always explicit. Council never falls back to the host's default route; a member with no model_hint is consulted with the FIRST entry of minerva_council_models, which is an alphabetical accident and a real cost.
- Nothing retries or resumes on its own. A partial round is a state to read and report, not an error to work around.
skills.preconditions: The council plugin is installed and RUNNING (minerva_plugin_list; minerva_plugin_start id="council" if not), and Minerva has at least one enabled provider with at least one model. A Council editor tab holds the record; if none is open, create one with minerva_create_plugin_editor {plugin_id: "council", editor_item_id: "new_mcouncil"} — the tab is the durable owner, and without one there is nothing to save into.
skills.outcome: The user has a council in their project, a consultation whose members' arguments and sources they can read in the Council tab, and — where they wanted one — a conclusion kept as a native note. The council can be exported and reused in another project without carrying this project's questions, transcripts or note links.
skills.steps:
Every command below is minerva_council_command with {request_id, command, base_revision, payload, wait_seconds?}. Take the current revision from `minerva_council_ping` first; omit base_revision on reads. wait_seconds is an optional top-level envelope field, never a payload field.

1. ORIENT. `minerva_council_ping` (liveness plus snapshot_revision) and `minerva_council_status` (the councils the loaded document holds, each session's status, chat binding, runs and kept outcomes). If no Council tab is open, open one first — see preconditions.

2. ASSEMBLE. Either start from a shipped council or build one.
   - Shipped: `minerva_council_presets` returns complete council_definition records (Decision Review, Second Opinion, and a source-grounded example). Replace the record's definition_id with a fresh one, then `definition.import` with payload {definition}. Import REFUSES an id the project already holds — that refusal is what stops it overwriting an edited council.
   - By hand: `definition.upsert` with a full record. Exactly one seat has role "chair". Members carry identity; seats carry responsibility in this council; they are separate on purpose.
   - Tell the user what a preset is: a starting point, not a fact about their situation.

3. GROUND (only if the user has material). `source.capture` with payload {definition_id, source_id, title, text, excerpts:[{anchor_id, quote}], author?, locator?, content_type?}: the ENGINE mints the next source_revision and derives the content hash, byte length and anchor spans from the text, so never compute or supply them. A quote that appears nowhere, or twice, is refused with a message saying which. Pass source_revision ONLY to repair an inventory entry that arrived without content, and then the text must hash to what that revision recorded. Then `member.upsert` with kind "simulant", a narrow scope, its stated gaps, and grounding [{source_id, source_revision}]. Moving a member to a newer capture later is `member.adopt_source` — an explicit act that leaves past answers reading what they actually read.

4. CHOOSE MODELS. `minerva_council_models` lists what the host actually has. Set each member's model_hint with `member.upsert`; a hint the host does not have is refused before the round spends anything.

5. CONSULT. A session belongs to a chat.
   - Preferred: tell the user to open a Minerva chat, pick Council as its provider, and ask there. If the project holds several councils, Council answers with a choice; picking one sends the directive `/council <definition_id>` as the next turn, and `/council-session <session_id>` points a chat at a consultation that already exists. A chat has exactly one session, and binding it to another MOVES the binding. From that chat, `/ask <member> <question>` asks one member alone — by display name, seat id, or the id of a claim they made, in which case it reaches whoever made it — and `/bench` lists the latest round's members, their models, their claims with the source/inference/unknown label, and each one's status without consulting anybody. An unknown or ambiguous name is refused with the seats; a human-held seat is never consulted.
   - Directly: `session.create` {session_id, definition_id, question, chat_id, context_snapshot?} — chat_id is required, so use the id of a real chat — then `run.start` {session_id, seat_ids, kind, prompt}. run.start CONSULTS THE MEMBERS and costs money. It answers within its bounded wait (1-25 s, default 20) with the run_id and what has arrived; a round that outruns the wait keeps going.

6. READ. `run.await` with payload {session_id, run_id} and top-level wait_seconds for a round still going, or `snapshot.get` for the whole record. Report each member's position, name where they disagree, and say which claims are supported by a cited source and which are the model's own inference — the record labels this per claim. Point the user at the Council tab for the arguments and their sources side by side.

7. FOLLOW UP, CANCEL, RETRY. `run.start` with addressed_seat_id (ask one member again) or addressed_claim_id (ask about one argument, routed to whoever made it) consults that seat ALONE. `run.cancel` {session_id, run_id} stops a round; a reply landing afterwards is recorded stale and moves nothing. `run.retry` {session_id, run_id, seat_ids?} starts a fresh round over the seats that did not answer.

8. KEEP. Create the note with minerva_create_note, then `outcome.retain` {session_id, run_id, contribution_id, note_ref, note_label?} to record the link. `outcome.mark_missing` records that a retained note could not be resolved, or that it is back; the link is kept either way.

9. REUSE. `definition.export` {definition_id, include_content, include_source_ids?} produces the portable council. It cannot carry a question, transcript, outcome, note id or chat id. It ALWAYS carries the source inventory — titles, authors, locators, hashes and anchor quotes — and carries source material only for the ids selected (omit the list for all, empty list for none). Tell the user which sources travelled and which were withheld; the reply names both. In the receiving project, `definition.import` reports every source that arrived without content, and `source.capture` against that revision repairs one.

SAVING: direct MCP commands and chat rounds change the backend store, and the backend announces each commit with the document's project_id and new revision. The panel holding THAT document reads the snapshot back, marks its tab changed and saves what the engine holds, so work driven entirely from here reaches the project through the open tab. Two things still need saying to the user: the tab has to be saved (or the project saved) like any other edited document, and if the panel reports that it could not read the council back — the backend stopped, say — what is on disk is the older copy and the newest results are still in the running backend. Do not claim work is saved while that message stands.

events.name: council.record_changed
events.description: Emitted after every commit the engine makes, including a chat turn or an MCP tool call with no panel in the exchange. payload: {project_id, snapshot_revision} — which document moved and to what revision. It carries no record and no authority: the panel that durably owns that document reads the snapshot back through its own exchange, and every other panel ignores it.
